app.name.where: MathTrail's name beside its logo heading its cards, such as a task's, and the name a screen reader gives a card that cannot be shown.
app.name.mind: A name: keep 'MathTrail' exactly as written, neither translated nor transliterated.

app.badge.where: The pill by MathTrail's name heading a lesson's cards, such as a task's: what MathTrail is, and the child's grade.
app.badge.mind: Two parts split by a middle dot: 'coach' as topic_choice.coach_short words it, and the grade as child.grade does; {grade} is a number from 1 to 6.

app.version.where: The word over the build's number in a small box at the end of a card's header, for an adult; a screen reader skips it.
app.version.mind: One short word: it sits over the number, which the card writes itself, in a box at most a third of the header wide.

child.grade.where: The pill under the child's pseudonym heading the progress and the profile's card, naming the child's school year.
child.grade.mind: {grade} is the child's school year, a number from 1 to 6; app.badge words the grade the same way.

task.profile_action.where: At the end of the line atop a lesson card, after the child's pseudonym; the line is a button that opens the profile and progress.
task.profile_action.mind: It never wraps, and a long one cuts the pseudonym short. first_run.start names it ('under Profile & progress'): use the same words.

task.label.where: The name a screen reader gives the part of the card holding the task, before it turns into how the answer went.

task.pick.where: The legend a screen reader alone hears over the task's five options; a press on one gives the answer at once.
task.pick.mind: Said to the child: where an imperative shows gender, a question such as 'Which answer is right?' instead.

task.checking.where: The words beside the option just pressed, with a spinner, while the service checks the answer.
task.checking.mind: One line inside the option's button, beside its text: a word or two.

task.hint.where: The Hint button under a task, a bulb alone, named to a screen reader and in a tooltip; also the label over the open hint.
task.hint.mind: A noun, not an order. task.hide_hint names the same button while the hint is open.

task.hide_hint.where: The name of the bulb-only Hint button while the hint is open, said to a screen reader and shown in a tooltip.
task.hide_hint.mind: Names the action, as an infinitive does, not an order to the child.

task.another.where: The Another task button: an arrows icon under an unanswered task, its words heard and in a tooltip; a worded button under the result.
task.another.mind: A press also puts these very words in the chat as the adult's message asking the model for a new task.

task.another_coming.where: A note at the card's foot once the chat has taken the ask for another task, in place of the buttons; it takes the focus.
task.another_coming.mind: A chat may hold the message for the adult to send, so it must not say the ask was sent. 'Below' is further down the chat.

task.answered_before.where: A note at the card's foot when the task already had an answer: the card shows that one, not the option just pressed.
task.answered_before.mind: Not 'you already answered': its past tense would show the child's gender in some languages.

picture.clock.where: The name a screen reader gives any clock-face picture, of a task or of its solution.
picture.clock.mind: Names the kind only, the same for every task: an analogue clock face with hands.

picture.table.where: The name a screen reader gives any picture of a table, of a task or of its solution.
picture.table.mind: Names the kind only: a small table of rows and cells, often a timetable, never the furniture.

picture.number_line.where: The name a screen reader gives any picture of a number line, of a task or of its solution.
picture.number_line.mind: Names the kind only: the school term for a line of evenly spaced, numbered ticks.

picture.row.where: The name a screen reader gives any picture of things in a row, of a task or of its solution.
picture.row.mind: Names the kind only: objects in a line, such as posts, trees or children in a queue.

picture.ring.where: The name a screen reader gives any picture of places in a ring, of a task or of its solution.
picture.ring.mind: Names the kind only: places round a circle, such as seats round a table, children in a circle or stops on a loop.

picture.grid.where: The name a screen reader gives any picture of a grid, of a task or of its solution.
picture.grid.mind: Names the kind only: a square grid whose rows and columns are named, so that a cell is B2.

picture.bars.where: The name a screen reader gives any picture of bars, of a task or of its solution.
picture.bars.mind: Names the kind only: bars drawn to one scale and cut into parts or segments, for fractions, ratios and shares.

picture.venn.where: The name a screen reader gives any picture of two overlapping groups, of a task or of its solution.
picture.venn.mind: Names the kind only: a Venn diagram of two groups. Plain words, as the English has, suit a child better than the term.

picture.balance.where: The name a screen reader gives any picture of a pan balance, of a task or of its solution.
picture.balance.mind: Names the kind only: scales with two pans, as weighing puzzles use, not a bathroom scale.

picture.containers.where: The name a screen reader gives any picture of containers, of a task or of its solution.
picture.containers.mind: Names the kind only: jugs, buckets or tanks of known sizes that water is poured between.

picture.piles.where: The name a screen reader gives any picture of piles, of a task or of its solution.
picture.piles.mind: Names the kind only: piles of stones, coins or counters, as a game starts.

picture.calendar.where: The name a screen reader gives any picture of a calendar page, of a task or of its solution.
picture.calendar.mind: Names the kind only: the calendar page of one month, its days set out in weeks.

picture.flags.where: The name a screen reader gives any picture of flags, of a task or of its solution.
picture.flags.mind: Names the kind only: flags of two or three coloured stripes, top to bottom.

picture.colors.where: The name a screen reader gives the key under a picture that paints, each colour beside its word; today only flags paint.

chat.not_sent.where: A note under a task's buttons, or under how its answer went, when the chat did not take the card's ask for another task.
chat.not_sent.mind: Say it of the card's message, impersonally: not 'you did not send', whose past tense shows gender in some languages.

task.answer_failed.where: A line under the task when the answer could not be checked; the options can be pressed again.
task.answer_failed.mind: 'Try again' is said to the child: where an imperative shows gender, 'let's try again' or an impersonal form.

task.closed.where: A line under a task pressed after a newer one was handed out: this one takes no answer, and its buttons are gone.
task.closed.mind: 'Closed' is said of the task. 'Further down the chat' is where the newest task's card is.

topic_choice.label.where: 'Topic:' before the chosen topic on the topic button under a task, and on the mark above a task given on that topic.
topic_choice.label.mind: A colon, or the language's own sign, since a name follows. A narrow card's button leaves it to a screen reader.

topic_choice.coach.where: The topic button's words after 'Topic:' on a wide card, with a spark icon, when the coach picks each task's topic.
topic_choice.coach.mind: Continues topic_choice.label, 'Topic: the coach chooses', hence the small letter. The coach is MathTrail itself, the 'Olympiad coach' of app.badge.

topic_choice.coach_short.where: The topic button's one word on a narrow card when the coach picks the topic; 'Topic:' before it is heard only.
topic_choice.coach_short.mind: The same coach as topic_choice.coach and app.badge, in a single word.

topic_choice.title.where: The heading of the topic choice, which the topic button opens under a task's buttons, beside a cross that closes it.

topic_choice.lead.where: A muted line under the topic choice's heading, saying what a press on a topic does.
topic_choice.lead.mind: A press asks for a new task at once, and the tasks after it keep to the topic. No full stop, as in the English.

topic_choice.close.where: The cross that closes the topic choice, named only to a screen reader.

topic_choice.coach_option.where: The first choice in the topic panel: it hands the topic back to the coach and asks for a new task at once.
topic_choice.coach_option.mind: The same coach as topic_choice.coach; it stands alone on its button, hence the capital.

topic_choice.coach_note.where: A muted note beside the coach's choice in the topic panel, saying what the coach picks topics by.
topic_choice.coach_note.mind: Continues the choice beside it, hence the small letter and no full stop. It speaks of the child as 'the child'.

topic_choice.recommended.where: The name of the topic panel's first row: up to three topics the review of the child's progress suggests.

topic_choice.from_grade.where: A muted note after a topic's name in the topic panel, for a topic taught from a grade above the child's.
topic_choice.from_grade.mind: {grade} is the school grade, 1 to 6, the topic is taught from; it follows the name, hence the small letter. A hint only: the topic can still be chosen.

topic_choice.ask.where: Not shown on the card: once a topic is chosen and saved, the card sends these words to the chat as the adult's message.
topic_choice.ask.mind: {topic} is the topic's name. It opens with task.another's words, as the English does, and reads as the adult's own request for a task on that topic.

topic_choice.ask_coach.where: Not shown on the card: once the coach's choice is saved, the card sends these words to the chat as the adult's message.
topic_choice.ask_coach.mind: It opens with task.another's words, as the English does; the coach is the one of topic_choice.coach.

topic_choice.saving.where: A note under the topic choice while the topic chosen is being saved; the card takes no other press meanwhile.

topic_choice.not_saved.where: A note under the topic choice when the topic chosen could not be saved; nothing goes to the chat.
topic_choice.not_saved.mind: Said to whoever pressed, who may be the child, as the Russian does; a form that speaks to nobody, as the German has, fits as well.

topic_choice.clear.where: The cross on the mark above a task given on the chosen topic, named only to a screen reader.
topic_choice.clear.mind: A press hands the topic back to the coach and asks for a new task. It names the action, as an infinitive does, not an order.

result.answers.where: The legend a screen reader alone hears over the task's options once the chat has taken the ask for another task.
result.answers.mind: Takes task.pick's place: the options no longer ask for a pick.

result.wrong.where: The verdict atop how the answer went, with a cross, after a wrong option.
result.wrong.mind: {correct} is the text of the right option, {picked} of the one chosen. Not 'you chose', whose past tense shows gender in some languages.

result.idk.where: The line atop how the answer went after 'I don't know', said in the chat; it has no right-or-wrong mark.
result.idk.mind: No verdict and no reproach: it only leads into the solution below. Not 'you didn't know'.

result.trap.where: The label of the note under a wrong verdict that explains the trap behind the option chosen.
result.trap.mind: A trap is the typical mistake a wrong option was built to catch; a word a child knows, as 'trap' is.

result.solution.where: The heading over the solution's numbered steps, on how the answer went.

result.right.where: The verdict atop how the answer went, with a tick, after the right option.
result.right.mind: {correct} is the text of the right option. Praise the answer, not the child: no word that agrees with the child.

result.rating.where: The name of a fact in the band at the foot of how the answer went; under it, how the rating moved.
result.rating.mind: The rating in the task's topic, a number; the same 'rating' as progress.overall_label.

result.rating_change.where: Under 'Rating in this topic': the rating before this answer, muted, then the rating after, in green or coral by the move.
result.rating_change.mind: {before} and {after} are numbers. The arrow points the way the language reads: ← in a right-to-left language.

result.trial.where: During the trial series: a fact's name at the foot of how the answer went, and the large title in the progress's rank place.
result.trial.mind: The first five tasks, which find where the child stands before any rank is given; the same series as progress.trial_ranks. Drawn large on the progress.

result.trial_progress.where: With 'Trial series', on how the answer went and on the progress: how many of the series' tasks are answered.

result.trap_again.where: A muted line under the explanation of the trap when the same mistake has come up in earlier answers.
result.trap_again.mind: Said of the mistake, not of the child: not 'you made it before', whose past tense shows gender in some languages.

result.label.where: The name a screen reader gives the part of the card showing how the answer went: verdict, trap, solution and rating.
result.label.mind: result.gone and result.untold speak of the same 'how the answer went'.

result.topic.where: A fact's name at the foot of how the answer went; its value, the task's topic, links to its page where the chat opens links.
result.topic.mind: Its value is a topic's name, such as 'Clocks'.

result.gone.where: The only line on a card the chat drew to show an answer, when a newer task has replaced that task.
result.gone.mind: 'No longer on the card' means a newer task took its place.

result.not_yet.where: The only line on a card the chat drew to show an answer, when the task has not been answered yet.

result.untold.where: The only line on a card the chat drew to show an answer, when the answer is kept but how it went is lost.
result.untold.mind: 'Counts' means it counts in the rating. Not 'you answered', whose past tense shows gender in some languages.

result.total_not.where: Under the picture of the solution, after a wrong option: the equality the solution comes to, then the option chosen.
result.total_not.mind: {total} is the equality, drawn large and always left to right, such as '2 + 2 + 2 = 6'; {picked} is the text of the wrong option.

waiting.title.where: The title over the list of steps on the card that waits for a task being prepared.

waiting.done.where: Said by a screen reader alone before each finished step in the list of a task being prepared.
waiting.done.mind: Read before a step's words, 'Done: Writing the task', so it keeps a colon or the language's own sign.

waiting.active.where: Said by a screen reader alone before the step under way in the list of a task being prepared.
waiting.active.mind: Read before a step's words, 'In progress: Writing the task', so it keeps a colon or the language's own sign.

waiting.waiting.where: Said by a screen reader alone before each step still to come in the list of a task being prepared.
waiting.waiting.mind: Of a step yet to come, not of someone who waits. Read before a step's words, so it keeps a colon or the language's own sign.

waiting.step.topic.where: The first step in the list of a task being prepared: a spinner while under way, a tick once done.
waiting.step.topic.mind: The same words stand while under way, with a spinner, and once ticked.

waiting.step.writing.where: The second step in the list of a task being prepared: the chat's model writing the task.
waiting.step.writing.mind: The same words stand while under way, with a spinner, and once ticked.

waiting.step.answers.where: The third step in the list of a task being prepared: the service checking the task.
waiting.step.answers.mind: 'Every answer' is each of the task's five options, checked before the task comes, not the child's answers.

waiting.step.ready.where: The last step in the list of a task being prepared, ticked just before the task takes the list's place.
waiting.step.ready.mind: Said of the task, or impersonally; one word where the language has one.

waiting.label.where: The name a screen reader gives the card while it waits for a task, or says why none came.

waiting.exhausted.where: The line on a card a task did not come to, after the last try at writing it failed the checks.
waiting.exhausted.mind: Blames no one. waiting.next_below follows it.

waiting.refused.where: The line on a card a task did not come to, after the model's try at writing it failed the service's checks.
waiting.refused.mind: A try is one attempt of the chat's model at writing the task; the same 'try' and 'checks' as waiting.rewriting.

waiting.rewriting.where: News under the steps of a task being prepared: a try failed the checks, and a new one is being written.

waiting.stale.where: The line on a card a task is not coming to, whatever ended its request.
waiting.stale.mind: True whatever ended the request. waiting.next_below follows it.

waiting.next_below.where: The line under a word that no task came: where the next task comes, and asking in the chat if none does.
waiting.next_below.mind: 'The next one' is the next task, in a card of its own further down the chat; the ask speaks to the adult.

waiting.cancelled.where: The line on the card of a task asked for, when the chat cancelled the call preparing it.
waiting.cancelled.mind: Blames no one. waiting.ask_in_chat follows it.

waiting.ask_in_chat.where: The line under 'This task wasn't finished.', sending the adult to ask for a task in the chat.

waiting.slow.where: News under the steps of a task being prepared, when two minutes pass with no news of it.

waiting.slow_detail.where: The line under 'The task is taking longer than usual.', sending the adult to the chat if the task never appears.
waiting.slow_detail.mind: 'It' is the task awaited; 'here' is this card.

waiting.limit.where: The first line on the card shown once the day's new tasks are used up.
waiting.limit.mind: No reproach and no number: only that new tasks come again tomorrow.

waiting.limit_detail.where: The line under the day's-limit line, pointing to the progress, opened from the card's top line, and to the last task above.
waiting.limit_detail.mind: 'Your progress' is the child's, opened from task.profile_action. Where 'you' shows gender, an impersonal 'one can', as the Russian has.

progress.label.where: Names the progress screen for a screen reader, also while it loads or when it fails to load.
progress.label.mind: The same words as the line at the top of a task's card that opens this screen, task.profile_action, which writes '&' for 'and'.

progress.back.where: The button at the top of the progress opened over a task's card; it closes the progress and returns to the task.

progress.back_plain.where: The button at the top of the progress that returns to the card under it, when that card shows no task.

progress.rank.where: The overall rank in large type at the top of the progress, and each topic's rank at the end of its row.
progress.rank.mind: {rank} is a number from 1 to 11, never a title. Keep it short: it also sits at the end of each topic's row.

progress.rank_of.where: Smaller text right after the large overall rank, saying how many ranks there are, so the two read 'Rank 3 of 11'.
progress.rank_of.mind: {total} is the number of ranks, 11. It continues progress.rank, so the two must read as one phrase.

progress.next_rank.where: The line under the bar of ranks: the next rank to reach, and how right answers and mistakes move the bar.
progress.next_rank.mind: {rank} is the next rank's number. 'The bar' is the bar of ranks above it: use the same word wherever a text names it.

progress.top_rank.where: The line under the bar of ranks, in place of the next rank, once the overall rank is the highest there is.

progress.share.where: Said by a screen reader in place of the drawn bar of ranks: how far through the current rank the child has come.
progress.share.mind: {share} is a percentage the card writes in the language's own digits and sign, such as '40%': add no sign of your own.

progress.grades.where: A short label under each bracket below the bar of ranks: the school grades whose tasks that run of ranks roughly matches.
progress.grades.mind: {from} and {to} are school years, such as 3 and 4, not marks. It stands under a bracket only about 75 px wide on a narrow card, so abbreviate as the English does.

progress.grades_ranks.where: Said by a screen reader in place of a bracket under the bar of ranks: the ranks it spans and the grades they match.
progress.grades_ranks.mind: {first} and {last} are rank numbers; {from} and {to} are school years.

progress.grades_ranks_here.where: Said by a screen reader in place of the bracket that holds the current rank: its ranks and the grades they match.
progress.grades_ranks_here.mind: {first} and {last} are rank numbers; {from} and {to} are school years. 'The current one' is the child's overall rank.

progress.grades_note.where: A small note under the grade brackets: what they show, and that they are a rough guide to olympiad tasks, not a school mark.
progress.grades_note.mind: 'Grades' are school years, as in progress.grades; 'a school mark' is what a teacher gives for work. The word for parents should mean neither only mothers nor only fathers.

progress.next_up.where: The label of the small box under the rank that names the topic of the next task.

progress.next_chosen.where: A small line in the 'Next up' box, under the topic, when it is the topic chosen for the lessons.
progress.next_chosen.mind: Impersonal: who chose the topic is not said, so no past tense agrees with a person.

progress.topics.where: The title of the folding section that lists the topics, each with its own rank and bar.

progress.topics_note.where: The line at the top of the list of topics, after the trial series, saying what each topic's bar shows.

progress.ahead.where: A small word before a topic's rank at the end of its row: the topic's rank is above the overall rank.
progress.ahead.mind: One of three words with progress.even and progress.behind. It describes the topic's rank, not the child, and sits beside 'Rank N'.

progress.behind.where: A small word before a topic's rank at the end of its row: the topic's rank is below the overall rank.
progress.behind.mind: One of three words with progress.ahead and progress.even. It describes the topic's rank, not the child: a plain fact, not a reproach.

progress.no_rank.where: The word at the end of each topic's row during the trial series, while no rank is given yet; the bar is drawn dashed.

progress.no_answers.where: The word at the end of a topic's row when the topic has no answers yet; its bar is drawn dashed.

progress.recent.where: The title of the folding section listing the latest five tasks and how each went, with a coloured dot for each by the title.

progress.mistakes.where: A heading over the mistakes that keep coming back: a folding section of its own during the trial series, then a part of the review.

progress.times.where: At the end of a repeating mistake's row, after up to five dots: how many times the mistake came up.
progress.times.mind: {count} is how many times the mistake came up. It never wraps, so keep it as short as the English.

progress.mastered.where: A green mark with a tick beside a topic's name in the list of topics, once the topic is mastered.
progress.mastered.mind: Said of the topic: an impersonal form or one that agrees with the topic, never with the child. The same word as review.reason_mastered.

progress.right.where: The green mark with a tick at the end of a recent answer's row, and what a screen reader says for its dot.
progress.right.mind: Said of the answer, never of the child: not 'you were right'.

progress.wrong.where: The mark with a cross at the end of a recent answer's row, and what a screen reader says for its dot.
progress.wrong.mind: Said of the answer, never of the child.

progress.loading.where: Said by a screen reader while the progress loads and a faint outline of the screen stands in its place.

progress.failed.where: Shown in place of the progress, under the child's name, when the progress could not be loaded.
progress.failed.mind: 'Go back' means the button at the top, progress.back or progress.back_plain. Where an imperative shows gender, use 'let's' or an impersonal form.

profile.label.where: The heading of the child's profile, beside its Edit button, on a profile card of an earlier chat.
profile.label.mind: Made of profile.card_label and progress.for_parent, in their words, split by a middle dot; 'the parent' is any adult who runs the lessons, named with no gender.

profile.edit.where: The button at the head of the child's profile, in the progress and on the profile card, that opens the form to change it.

progress.overall_label.where: Names, for a screen reader, the block with the overall rank across all topics, its bar and the lines under it.

progress.again.where: The text in the 'Next up' box when the next task goes back to the topic just answered wrongly.
progress.again.mind: {topic} is a topic's name as its own dictionary entry writes it, with a capital: keep it first, in a form that needs no other case.

progress.skipped.where: The grey mark at the end of a recent task's row when it got no answer, and what a screen reader says for its dot.
progress.skipped.mind: Said of the task, never in a form that agrees with the child.

progress.skipped_count.where: A small note under the list of recent answers: how many tasks in all were left without an answer.
progress.skipped_count.mind: {count} is a number of tasks. Keep it impersonal: who left them without an answer is not said.

progress.trial_ranks.where: The line under the trial series' bar of five steps, in place of the next rank: ranks come once those tasks are done.
progress.trial_ranks.mind: {total} is the number of tasks in the trial series, five. The text has no plural forms, so write it for that number.

progress.for_parent.where: Small text beside the title of the folding section with the child's profile, saying the section is for the parent.
progress.for_parent.mind: A word for 'parent' that means neither only a mother nor only a father.

progress.period.where: Said by a screen reader as the name of the two-part switch above the rank, which chooses the period the changes cover.
progress.period.mind: Names the switch whose two parts are progress.period_task and progress.period_week.

progress.period_task.where: The first part of the switch above the rank: shows the changes since the last task answered.
progress.period_task.mind: It shares one row with progress.period_week, half the card each: keep it a word or two.

progress.period_week.where: The second part of the switch above the rank: shows the changes over the past seven days.
progress.period_week.mind: The last seven days up to today, not the calendar week. It shares one row with progress.period_task: keep it a word or two.

progress.week_rank_up.where: A line under the bar of ranks, green after an up arrow: over the past week the overall rank went up.
progress.week_rank_up.mind: {from} and {to} are rank numbers, before and now; keep the arrow between them. Nothing says who moved, so nothing agrees with the child.

progress.week_forward.where: A line under the bar of ranks, green after an up arrow: over the past week the bar moved on within the rank.
progress.week_forward.mind: The bar is the subject, so a past tense agrees with the bar, never with the child. The same word for the bar as in progress.next_rank.

progress.week_same.where: A plain line under the bar of ranks: over the past week the bar did not move.
progress.week_same.mind: The bar is the subject, never the child. The same word for the bar as in progress.next_rank.

progress.week_back.where: A line under the bar of ranks, coral after a down arrow: over the past week the bar moved back within the rank.
progress.week_back.mind: The bar is the subject, never the child; calm, not a reproach. The same word for the bar as in progress.next_rank.

progress.week_rank_down.where: A line under the bar of ranks, coral after a down arrow: over the past week the overall rank went down.
progress.week_rank_down.mind: {from} and {to} are rank numbers, before and now; keep the arrow between them. 'The rank below' says it gently.

progress.week_untold.where: A plain line under the bar of ranks when there is nothing yet to measure the past week's change from.

progress.task_rank_up.where: A line under the bar of ranks, green after an up arrow: the last task answered raised the overall rank.
progress.task_rank_up.mind: {from} and {to} are rank numbers, before and after the last task; keep the arrow between them.

progress.task_forward.where: A line under the bar of ranks, green after an up arrow: the last task answered moved the bar on within the rank.
progress.task_forward.mind: The task is the subject, not the child. The same word for the bar as in progress.next_rank.

progress.task_same.where: A plain line under the bar of ranks: the last task answered did not move the bar.
progress.task_same.mind: The task is the subject, not the child. The same word for the bar as in progress.next_rank.

progress.task_back.where: A line under the bar of ranks, coral after a down arrow: the last task answered moved the bar back within the rank.
progress.task_back.mind: The task is the subject, not the child; calm, not a reproach. The same word for the bar as in progress.next_rank.

progress.task_rank_down.where: A line under the bar of ranks, coral after a down arrow: the last task answered took the overall rank down.
progress.task_rank_down.mind: {from} and {to} are rank numbers, before and after the last task; keep the arrow between them. 'The rank below' says it gently.

progress.task_untold.where: A plain line under the bar of ranks when there is nothing yet to measure the last task's change from.

progress.even.where: A small word before a topic's rank at the end of its row: the topic's rank equals the overall rank.
progress.even.mind: One of three words with progress.ahead and progress.behind: level with the overall rank.

progress.note_rank_up.where: Green words after an up arrow, before a topic's rank: the topic reached a new rank in the period chosen on the switch.
progress.note_rank_up.mind: It takes the place of ahead, even or behind, beside 'Rank N': a word or two, said of the topic.

progress.note_forward.where: A green word after an up arrow, before a topic's rank: its bar moved forward within the rank in the period chosen.
progress.note_forward.mind: It takes the place of ahead, even or behind, beside 'Rank N': one word, as in English.

progress.note_back.where: A coral word after a down arrow, before a topic's rank: its bar moved back within the rank in the period chosen.
progress.note_back.mind: It takes the place of ahead, even or behind, beside 'Rank N': one word, as in English.

progress.note_rank_down.where: Coral words after a down arrow, before a topic's rank: the topic went down a rank in the period chosen on the switch.
progress.note_rank_down.mind: A gentle 'the rank below', as in progress.week_rank_down; a word or two, said of the topic.

progress.note_new.where: Green words after an up arrow, before a topic's rank: the topic was answered for the first time in the period chosen.
progress.note_new.mind: New to the child's answers, not new in MathTrail; a word or two.

progress.moved_up.where: Said by a screen reader by the title 'Topics', where only an up arrow and a number show how many topics moved forward.
progress.moved_up.mind: {count} is a number of topics; a topic answered for the first time counts too. Read with progress.moved_down as one list.

progress.moved_down.where: Said by a screen reader by the title 'Topics', where only a down arrow and a number show how many topics slipped back.
progress.moved_down.mind: {count} is a number of topics. Read after progress.moved_up as one list.

progress.legend_gain.where: In the key above the list of topics, beside a sample of green stripes: what green stripes on a bar mean.
progress.legend_gain.mind: One short word, the opposite of progress.legend_loss.

progress.legend_loss.where: In the key above the list of topics, beside a sample of coral stripes: what coral stripes on a bar mean.
progress.legend_loss.mind: A mild word for a step back, the opposite of progress.legend_gain.

progress.legend_week.where: Ends the key above the list of topics, after a dot: the stripes show the change over the past week.
progress.legend_week.mind: The same period as progress.period_week: the last seven days.

progress.legend_task.where: Ends the key above the list of topics, after a dot: the stripes show the change since the last task.

progress.link_refused.where: Under a linked name, a topic or a group of topics, when the chat did not open its page; the page's address follows to copy.
progress.link_refused.mind: 'The chat' is the chat app the card is shown in. The address follows on its own line, left to right, for the reader to copy.

review.title.where: The title of the folding section with the review of the topics, shown once the trial series is over.
review.title.mind: An assessment of how the topics stand, not a revision of material.

review.summary.where: Small text beside the title 'Review', naming what the section holds.

review.strong.where: A green heading in the review over the topics that go well, each with why.
review.strong.mind: The same idea as 'a strength' in review.step_begin.

review.develop.where: A coral heading in the review over the topics to work on, each with why.
review.develop.mind: A heading, not an instruction: a noun or an infinitive, as the Russian and German have it.

review.early.where: A grey heading in the review over the topics with too few answers to judge yet.

review.next.where: A heading in the review over the numbered steps of the plan, the review's last part.
review.next.mind: A heading with no 'you' in it.

review.reason_mastered.where: A reason under a strong topic's name in the review: the topic is mastered.
review.reason_mastered.mind: Said of the topic, never in a form that agrees with the child. Reasons are joined into one line, so it ends with its own full stop.

review.reason_high.where: A reason under a strong topic's name in the review: it stands well above the child's overall level.
review.reason_high.mind: Reasons are joined into one line, so it ends with its own full stop.

review.reason_rose.where: A reason under a strong topic's name in the review: it rose clearly over the past seven days.
review.reason_rose.mind: 'The past week' is the last seven days, as in progress.period_week. Reasons are joined into one line, so it ends with its own full stop.

review.reason_low.where: A reason under the name of a topic to develop: it stands well below the child's overall level.
review.reason_low.mind: Reasons are joined into one line, so it ends with its own full stop.

review.reason_failures.where: A reason under the name of a topic to develop: its answers were wrong several times in a row.
review.reason_failures.mind: Said of the answers, not the child. Reasons are joined into one line, so it ends with its own full stop.

review.reason_hints.where: A reason under the name of a topic to develop: the hint was used in many of its recent answers.
review.reason_hints.mind: Impersonal, 'the hint is often needed', as in Russian and German, so no form shows the child's gender. 'The hint' is task.hint's word.

review.reason_trap.where: A reason under the name of a topic to develop: one mistake keeps coming back in its answers.
review.reason_trap.mind: {trap} is a mistake's name, a phrase such as 'Off by one when counting gaps' that starts with a capital: keep it first. It ends with its own full stop.

review.reason_fell.where: A reason under the name of a topic to develop: it fell back clearly over the past seven days.
review.reason_fell.mind: 'The past week' is the last seven days, as in progress.period_week. Calm, not a reproach; it ends with its own full stop.

review.moving.where: Added after the reasons under a topic to develop, when the latest answer in that topic was right.
review.moving.mind: Joined after the reasons into one line, so it ends with its own full stop.

review.early_note.where: A small line under the names of the topics too early to judge, saying why they get no verdict yet.
review.early_note.mind: 'These' are the topics named on the line above it.

review.step_rhythm.where: A numbered step of the plan, under the name of a topic that fell back: a little practice each day.
review.step_rhythm.mind: 'The bar' is the topic's bar, the same word as in progress.next_rank. Advice with no 'you' in it.

review.step_practice.where: A numbered step of the plan, under the name of a topic that stands low or was answered wrongly in a row.
review.step_practice.mind: MathTrail stays as written. 'The child' is said in general, with no pronoun after it.

review.step_unaided.where: A numbered step of the plan, under the name of a topic named only for leaning on the hint.
review.step_unaided.mind: Russian and German give it as an infinitive, addressed to nobody: avoid an imperative, which some languages mark for gender. 'The hint' is task.hint's word.

review.step_begin.where: The last numbered step of the plan, under the name of a new topic to begin, naming the strong topic it builds on.
review.step_begin.mind: {base} is a strong topic's name as its own dictionary entry writes it, with a capital: keep it first, in a form that needs no other case.

profile.card_label.where: The title of the folding section of the progress that holds the profile and the parent's data; also a screen reader's name for the profile card.

profile.grade.where: The name of the grade among the profile's details, and the label of the grade's list on the profile's form.
profile.grade.mind: The same word for the school year as child.grade and app.badge.

profile.grade_note.where: A note under the grade, among the profile's details and on its form, saying that changing it moves none of the ratings.
profile.grade_note.mind: 'Only a label': the grade is kept as information alone, and changing it leaves every rating as it was.

profile.interests.where: The name of the child's interests among the profile's details, and the heading of the interests on the profile's form.
profile.interests.mind: The child's hobbies, which tasks are themed on; the 'them' of problem.entry_length refers to this word.

profile.not_yet.where: The name of the skills the child has not met at school yet, among the profile's details and over their tick boxes on the form.
profile.not_yet.mind: Tasks leave these skills out. Word it with no form that shows the child's gender: an impersonal or plural form, as the Russian has.

profile.language.where: The name of the language of the lessons among the profile's details, and the label of its list on the profile's form.
profile.language.mind: The language of the tasks, the cards and the model's words; first_run.fill names it the same way.

profile.language_chat.where: The first choice in the form's list of languages, and the value shown when none is chosen: the lessons then follow the chat's language.
profile.language_chat.mind: Means the lessons follow the chat's own language (the Russian says 'as in the chat'); keep it short, as a narrow list cuts it.

profile.country.where: The name of the family's country among the profile's details, and the label of its list on the profile's form.
profile.country.mind: The country the family lives in.

profile.country_note.where: A note under the country, among the profile's details and on the form, saying it is optional and what it is used for.
profile.country_note.mind: Exact in meaning: giving it is optional, and it serves only to count families by country, without names.

profile.region.where: The name of the US state among the profile's details, and the label of its list on the form, shown only for the United States.
profile.region.mind: A state of the United States, the only country the form asks a region of; the states are listed by their English names.

profile.signin_country_off.where: A tick box at the end of the profile's form that leaves the country the parent signs in from out of what is counted.
profile.signin_country_off.mind: The parent's own words, in the first person: keep 'I' free of gender, as a present tense is. The country is the one the sign-in comes from.

profile.none.where: The value of an empty detail of the profile, and the first choice, meaning none, in the form's lists of countries and states.
profile.none.mind: Used for the interests, the skills, the country and the state alike, so it must not agree with any one of their names.

profile.not_saved.where: The verdict at the top of a profile card of an earlier chat when the change asked for was refused, until one is saved.
profile.not_saved.mind: Say it of the change, impersonally: not 'you did not save', whose past tense shows gender in some languages.

profile.not_saved_detail.where: The line under the verdict profile.not_saved on the profile card, and under first_run.not_created on the first-run card, sending the parent to the chat.
profile.not_saved_detail.mind: It must fit both a change not saved and a first profile not made.

profile.form_label.where: The name a screen reader gives the form, opened by the Edit button, in which the parent changes the child's profile.
profile.form_label.mind: A name for the form rather than an instruction: a noun or an infinitive, as the Russian and the German have it.

profile.pseudonym.where: The label of the box on the profile's form where the child's pseudonym is typed.
profile.pseudonym.mind: The word first_run.pseudonym_label uses: a made-up name the child is known by, never a real one.

profile.pseudonym_note.where: The note under the pseudonym's box on the profile's form, stating the rule of the pseudonym.
profile.pseudonym_note.mind: The rule of the pseudonym, exact in meaning: never the child's real name.

profile.interest_new.where: The label of the box on the profile's form where a new interest is typed; only a screen reader says it.

profile.interest_add.where: The button beside the box for a new interest, which adds the interest typed to the child's interests.

profile.interest_remove.where: What a screen reader says for the cross on each interest's chip on the form, which takes that interest out.
profile.interest_remove.mind: {interest} is the interest as the parent typed it, in any language; set it in the language's own quotation marks, as the Russian does.

profile.interests_full.where: A note under the interests on the form once the list is as long as a profile allows and the box to type in shuts.
profile.interests_full.mind: No number in the text: it says the list is as full as a profile allows, which is ten interests.

profile.save.where: The main button at the foot of the profile's form, which saves the changes made.

profile.cancel.where: The button beside Save at the foot of the profile's form, which closes it without saving anything.

profile.saving.where: The note under the form's buttons while the changes are on their way to be saved.

profile.saved.where: The note under the head of the child's profile, by the Edit button, once a change from the form is saved.

profile.saved_language.where: The note under the head of the child's profile, by the Edit button, once a change of the lessons' language is saved.
profile.saved_language.mind: The card itself goes on in the language it was drawn in; the new language comes with the next task's card.

profile.save_failed.where: The note under the form's buttons when a save did not go through; the form stays open, to save again.
profile.save_failed.mind: Say it of the change, impersonally: not 'you did not save', whose past tense shows gender in some languages.

profile.save_refused.where: The note under the form's buttons when the service refused the change; each refused field says why under it.
profile.save_refused.mind: 'The fields marked' are those with an error under them, the problem.* texts.

profile.gone.where: Said in place of the profile's details, or under the choice of a task's topic, when the profile turns out to be deleted.
profile.gone.mind: The profile's file was deleted since the card was drawn; a new profile is made by asking in the chat.

problem.required.where: An error under a field of the profile's form that was saved empty, in practice the pseudonym.

problem.too_long.where: An error under a field of the profile's form whose text the service found longer than a profile allows.
problem.too_long.mind: It may stand under any field, so it must not agree with one field's name; 'it' is the text in the field.

problem.too_many.where: An error under the interests, or the ticked skills, on the profile's form when they hold more than a profile allows.
problem.too_many.mind: It stands under the interests or the ticked skills, so 'take some out' must fit removing interests and unticking skills alike.

problem.entry_length.where: An error under the interests on the profile's form when one of them is empty or longer than an interest may be.
problem.entry_length.mind: 'Them' are the interests listed above it: agree with the word profile.interests uses.

problem.out_of_range.where: An error under the grade on the profile's form when the grade sent is not one of those the list offers.

problem.not_in_catalog.where: An error under the ticked skills on the profile's form when one of them is a skill MathTrail no longer has.
problem.not_in_catalog.mind: 'These' are the ticked skills above; the unknown one shows by a code, not a name. 'Untick' is clearing its box.

problem.not_a_language.where: An error under the language of the lessons on the profile's form when the service reads no language in it.

problem.other.where: An error under a field of the profile's form for any refusal the card has no words of its own for.
problem.other.mind: Generic on purpose: it must fit any field of the form.

data.label.where: The heading of the part under the profile that tells the parent where its file is, and how to delete it or cut MathTrail off.
data.label.mind: 'Your' is the parent's: the profile's data, kept in the parent's own Google Drive.

data.where.where: The heading of the first item of the parent's data, over the text that says where the profile's file is.
data.where.mind: A heading naming the question its text answers, never a command: nothing in this part can be pressed.

data.export_where.where: The text answering 'Where the profile is', naming the profile's file and its folder in the parent's Google Drive.
data.export_where.mind: {file} and {folder} are names in Drive, shown as they are. Name Google Drive as Google does in the language (Russian: Google Диск).

data.export_file.where: The text answering 'Where the profile is' when no folder is named, naming the profile's file in the parent's Google Drive.
data.export_file.mind: {file} is the file's name in Drive, shown as it is; worded as data.export_where, less the folder.

data.others.where: A note under where the profile is, naming other files in the parent's Drive that hold a profile too.
data.others.mind: {files} are the other files' names, already joined into a list in the language's own way.

data.how_delete.where: The heading of the item of the parent's data that says how to delete the profile.
data.how_delete.mind: 'It' is the profile. A heading naming the question its text answers, never a command: nothing here can be pressed.

data.delete_how.where: The text answering 'How to delete it': how to delete the profile for good.
data.delete_how.mind: Exact in meaning: with the file deleted and Drive's bin emptied, no copy of the profile is left anywhere. Name the bin as Google Drive does in the language.

data.how_cut_off.where: The heading of the item of the parent's data that says how to cut MathTrail off from the parent's Google account.
data.how_cut_off.mind: The access is MathTrail's, to the parent's Google account. A heading naming a question, never a command: nothing here can be pressed.

data.access_how.where: The text answering 'How to cut off access': where in the Google account to take MathTrail's access away.
data.access_how.mind: Name the page as Google's account settings do in the language: the one listing third-party apps with access. 'It' is MathTrail.

data.how_remove.where: The heading of the last item of the parent's data, which says how to remove MathTrail from the chat.
data.how_remove.mind: 'The app' is MathTrail in the chat. A heading naming a question, never a command: nothing here can be pressed.

data.remove_how.where: The text answering 'How to remove the app': where to disconnect MathTrail.
data.remove_how.mind: 'Your chat' is the chat app the lessons run in, such as Claude or ChatGPT; MathTrail is disconnected in its settings.

first_run.label.where: The name a screen reader gives the first-run card, which tells an adult with no profile yet what MathTrail is and how to start.
first_run.label.mind: A greeting that must not show the reader's gender (not Spanish 'Bienvenido'); MathTrail stays as written.

first_run.lead.where: The opening paragraph of the first-run card, under MathTrail's name: what MathTrail is, and who sets it up.
first_run.lead.mind: Name the parent and the tutor with words that show no gender where the language has them, as German 'ein Elternteil oder eine Lehrkraft'.

first_run.pseudonym_label.where: The small heading of the first-run card's note on the rule of the pseudonym.

first_run.pseudonym.where: The text of the first-run card's note on the pseudonym, under first_run.pseudonym_label.
first_run.pseudonym.mind: The privacy rule, exact in meaning: a pseudonym only, never a real name, a birth date or a school.

first_run.fill_label.where: The small heading of the first-run card's note on what the chat will ask to make the profile.

first_run.fill.where: The text of the first-run card's note on what the chat will ask: the details it needs, then those it may take.
first_run.fill.mind: 'They' is the child: word it so no gender shows, as the Russian does. Name the details as profile.interests, profile.not_yet and profile.language do.

first_run.data_label.where: The small heading of the first-run card's note on where the profile is kept.

first_run.data.where: The text of the first-run card's note on where the profile is kept.
first_run.data.mind: Exact in meaning: the profile is one file in the parent's own Google Drive, and MathTrail stores nothing itself. Name Google Drive as Google does in the language.

first_run.start_label.where: The small heading of the first-run card's last note, on how to start.

first_run.start.where: The text of the first-run card's last note: how to get a profile made, and where to change it later.
first_run.start.mind: 'Profile & progress' is the line at the top of a task's card: use the words of task.profile_action exactly.

first_run.not_created.where: The verdict at the top of a first-run card of an earlier chat when making the profile was refused.
first_run.not_created.mind: Say it of the profile, impersonally: not 'you did not create it', whose past tense shows gender in some languages.

card.unreadable.where: The only words on a card the widget cannot draw, under MathTrail's name, pointing to the chat, which says the same.
card.unreadable.mind: The chat's own message carries what the card would have shown, so the card points there.

group.logic.where: The name of the group Logic: a heading in the topic choice, linking to its part of the site's page of topics.
group.logic.mind: Where the site speaks the language, it matches the group's heading on the site's page of topics.

group.counting.where: The name of the group Counting and enumeration: a heading in the topic choice, linking to its part of the site's page of topics.
group.counting.mind: Where the site speaks the language, it matches the group's heading on the site's page of topics. 'Enumeration' is the listing of every option, as in topic.combinatorics.enumeration.

group.time.where: The name of the group Time: a heading in the topic choice, linking to its part of the site's page of topics.
group.time.mind: Where the site speaks the language, it matches the group's heading on the site's page of topics.

group.numbers.where: The name of the group Numbers with a trick: a heading in the topic choice, linking to its part of the site's page of topics.
group.numbers.mind: Where the site speaks the language, it matches the group's heading on the site's page of topics. Holds arithmetic with a trick, parity and divisibility: numbers with a catch to see through.

group.parts.where: The name of the group Parts of a whole: a heading in the topic choice, linking to its part of the site's page of topics.
group.parts.mind: Where the site speaks the language, it matches the group's heading on the site's page of topics. 'Part' and 'whole' are the words of trap.part_whole_swap.

group.games.where: The name of the group Strategies and games: a heading in the topic choice, linking to its part of the site's page of topics.
group.games.mind: Where the site speaks the language, it matches the group's heading on the site's page of topics. Holds winning-strategy games and weighing and pouring, so 'strategies' are plans of moves.

topic.logic.ordering.where: The name of the topic Ordering: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.logic.ordering.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. Here it is putting in order from comparisons: who is older, who stands behind whom.

topic.logic.knights_liars.where: The name of the topic Knights and liars: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.logic.knights_liars.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. Knights always tell the truth, liars always lie; use these puzzles' name in the language's olympiad books.

topic.combinatorics.enumeration.where: The name of the topic Enumeration: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.combinatorics.enumeration.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. Counting every option by listing them all, by the method's name in olympiad books.

topic.counting.gaps.where: The name of the topic Gaps and boundaries: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.counting.gaps.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. Fence-post tasks, such as trees in a row; 'gaps' is the word of trap.off_by_one.

topic.time.clocks.where: The name of the topic Clocks: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.time.clocks.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. The time of day and how long things last, as a clock shows them.

topic.time.calendar.where: The name of the topic Calendar and age: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.time.calendar.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form.

topic.pigeonhole.basic.where: The name of the topic Pigeonhole principle: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.pigeonhole.basic.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. Use the principle's established name in the language's school maths: Dirichlet's in Russian, Schubfachprinzip in German.

topic.parity.alternation.where: The name of the topic Parity and alternation: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.parity.alternation.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. Parity is even and odd, the words of skill.even_odd; alternation is things taking turns along a row.

topic.arithmetic.tricks.where: The name of the topic Arithmetic with a trick: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.arithmetic.tricks.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. Tricky sums with a short way through, and 'I thought of a number' puzzles.

topic.algorithms.weighing_pouring.where: The name of the topic Weighing and pouring: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.algorithms.weighing_pouring.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. Puzzles of weighings on a balance and pourings between jugs, by the names olympiad books give them.

topic.fractions.parts.where: The name of the topic Parts and shares: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.fractions.parts.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. A share here is a fraction of a whole, such as a third of the class.

topic.percent.basic.where: The name of the topic Percentages: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.percent.basic.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. Its English is that of skill.percentages, and the two may share their words.

topic.ratio.sharing.where: The name of the topic Ratios and sharing: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.ratio.sharing.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. Sharing an amount in a given ratio; 'ratio' is the word of skill.ratios.

topic.geometry.grid.where: The name of the topic Figures on a square grid: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.geometry.grid.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. The squared paper of school exercise books, with figures drawn along its lines.

topic.number.divisibility.where: The name of the topic Divisibility and remainders: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.number.divisibility.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. The school terms, as in skill.divisibility_rules and skill.division_with_remainder.

topic.logic.sets.where: The name of the topic Overlapping groups: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.logic.sets.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. Two groups that overlap, drawn as overlapping circles; said in plain words, not as sets.

topic.games.strategy.where: The name of the topic Games with a winning strategy: a result's band, the progress, the topic choice, and its page's heading on the site.
topic.games.strategy.mind: Also a link and a button, and set unchanged into sentences such as topic_choice.ask, so it keeps its dictionary form. Two players take turns; 'winning strategy' is the term of the language's olympiad books.

skill.addition.where: The skill Addition: a tick under 'Not at school yet' on the profile's form, and listed under it in the profile.

skill.subtraction.where: The skill Subtraction: a tick under 'Not at school yet' on the profile's form, and listed under it in the profile.

skill.multiplication.where: The skill Multiplication: a tick under 'Not at school yet' on the profile's form, and listed under it in the profile.
